training.note: The epoch-5 weights scored 0.01431 and were discarded in favour of epoch 3.333 at 0.01420.

curve_note: Training was stopped once at epoch 1.94 on a single-eval rise that turned out to be noise; resuming improved eval_loss by a further 32%. Two consecutive rises, not one, is the rule that would have avoided that.

held_out_metrics.note: Original 2026-08 run, adapter's raw numerics. Superseded by held_out_metrics_2026_09_17.

end_to_end_vs_xgboost.note: Errors in lead_score and engagement_score barely move the deal score, because the regressor leans on the categoricals and those are 100% accurate.

known_weakness.lead_score: 40% field accuracy, unchanged across 5 epochs. It is a weighted sum the model must land exactly; an 8B model does not do reliable multi-term arithmetic. Both lead_score and engagement_score are pure functions of fields the model gets right, so they should be recomputed after generation in serve.py rather than trained harder. That would also lift exact_state from 33% to roughly 85%.
known_weakness.engagement_score: 80% field accuracy, same cause, simpler formula.
known_weakness.status: Resolved at serve time: server/main.py and eval/evaluate.py recompute lead_score and engagement_score via apply_derived_fields(); use evaluate.py --raw to see the adapter's own arithmetic.

base_model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (ai/base-model/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; trained from the old ../Llama3_CRM/models copy of the same weights)
chat_template: project-owned, carries {% generation %} markers so assistant_only_loss masks the prompt

held_out_metrics_2026_09_17.scored_as: served: coerce_state() then apply_derived_fields() recomputes lead_score/engagement_score
held_out_metrics_2026_09_17.caveat: 72% of held-out meeting-note sentences appear verbatim in the training split (template generator), so this measures fit to the generator, not accuracy on real CRM notes. Validate on hand-labelled real meetings before trusting it.
